correctness.rationale: For every m>=3 and t>0 the proof explicitly expands the powered shortest-path quadratic form on the entire zero-sum space as an (m-1)-fold 2x2 fluctuation form plus a scalar radial form. The fluctuation determinant is strictly positive throughout 0<p<2 by concavity, so only the radial scalar can vanish. It is negative at p=1 and positive at p=2; two distinct zeros contradict the published strict-downward-propagation theorem because each zero is a nonstrict negative-type endpoint. The derived equality vector, Gram ranks, strict monotonicity, and three asymptotic limits use algebraic identities, convexity and standard local expansions with explicit domains. The actual standalone verifier independently reconstructs shortest paths, checks 576 exact rational quadratic identities and 105 numerical inertia profiles; these are corroborations, not proofs for infinitely many parameters.

originality.rationale: Targeted comparison distinguishes the variable-powered shortest-path metric of a positively weighted complete-graph corona from existing first-power quadratic embedding constants for corona graphs, Sánchez general-purpose finite-metric criteria, Li--Weston strictness propagation, and the same graph family’s general-position polynomial. Neither the exact root equation nor both sharp pendant-length asymptotics follow from the compared statements without new argument. The accessible own-claim record includes a two-pendant clique, double stars, metric stars and bridge barbells; none is the complete corona with arbitrary common positive pendant length. Novelty is best-knowledge, qualified by possible unindexed work.
residual_risks: Unindexed work may have the same equation under a different graph or metric name; neither semantic search nor inspected primary references prove global uniqueness.

value.rationale: Complete graph coronas with one pendant per vertex are a standard graph construction, and varying a common pendant-edge length is a canonical metric deformation. A complete p-negative-type classification, unique critical geometric obstruction, exact Hilbert dimensions and a logarithmically slow collapse to exponent 2 illuminate how metric snowflakes behave under pendant-edge degeneration. The collapsed limit is an equilateral m-point quotient with infinite exponent, so the explicit singularity is geometrically substantive, not a routine renaming of the fixed-length clique or star cases. The large-length star limit and fixed-length branching law provide additional natural comparison regimes. No arbitrary slices or unsupported downstream claims are used.
